title: Demystifying Next.js 15 Caching: Server Actions, fetch, and Dynamic Boundaries
description: A practical guide to Next.js 15 cache defaults, handling revalidatePath properly in Server Actions, and avoiding unexpected stale data.

content.heading: The Shift in Next.js 15 Caching Defaults
paragraphs: In Next.js 14 and earlier, fetch requests were cached by default (force-cache), often leading to confusing scenarios where mutations appeared to execute on the server but the client continued displaying obsolete UI data.

Next.js 15 changed this paradigm: fetch requests, GET Route Handlers, and client navigations default to 'no-store' unless explicitly configured. While this improves data freshness out-of-the-box, developers must understand how to selectively cache expensive operations without introducing stale-reads after Server Actions.

content.heading: Diagnosing Stale UI After Server Actions
paragraphs: When a user submits a form or performs a critical mutation, the UI must immediately reflect the new state. A common bug is updating the database in a Server Action but forgetting to invalidate either the route segment or the specific tag.
bullets: Always call revalidatePath(path) or revalidateTag(tag) inside the Server Action after successful database persistence.
Return structured outcome objects { success: boolean, error?: string } rather than relying solely on redirects.
Ensure optimistic updates use React 19's useOptimistic hook when instant feedback is required.

content.heading: Key Takeaways for Full-Stack Systems
paragraphs: By decoupling data mutation from layout rendering and leveraging explicit cache tags (revalidateTag), Next.js applications remain blazingly fast while guaranteeing data integrity across collaborative and multi-user views.

title: Optimizing List Rendering and State Updates in React Native and Expo
description: How to diagnose frame drops in large mobile feeds, replace unoptimized ScrollViews with FlashList or memoized FlatLists, and isolate state mutations.

content.heading: The Problem & Symptoms
paragraphs: When rendering hundreds of catalog items or transactions in React Native apps built with Expo, users often report stuttering during fast scrolling, UI thread freezes, or high memory consumption on lower-end devices.

The root cause typically stems from rendering un-virtualized items in a standard ScrollView, creating inline arrow functions within renderItem, or passing non-primitive unstable props that trigger cascades of re-renders.

content.heading: Diagnosis & Profiling
paragraphs: To locate the rendering bottleneck:
1. Use the React DevTools Profiler in Flipper or the Expo development build to identify which list cells re-render during scroll.
2. Check if parent state updates (such as a search input or a filter toggle) cause the entire list data array to be recreated with fresh object references.
bullets: Identify unneeded cell re-renders using React.memo with custom equality comparison.
Check windowSize, maxToRenderPerBatch, and removeClippedSubviews on FlatList.
Ensure keyExtractor returns a stable unique string (never index).

paragraphs: Isolate the cell component and ensure callbacks are stabilized with useCallback. Here is a production-tested pattern for high-performance listing:

content.heading: Verification & Verification Checklist
paragraphs: Verify the fix by running an FPS monitor in the Expo development client. Stable 60 FPS scrolling should be achieved across both Android and iOS without ballooning memory usage.
bullets: Verify UI thread remains at 58-60 FPS under rapid swipe.
Ensure memory usage levels off rather than climbing monotonically.
Confirm layout calculations don't shift when new items stream into view.
